hypothesis: A lower mobile back-buffer cost preserves story quality while reducing missed refreshes.
treatment: DPR 1.5 then 1.25; separately MSAA off
locked_variables: device, browser, viewport, revision, input trace, warm cache
objective_measures: frame interval percentiles; >1.5x/>2x misses; streak; backing pixels; GL calls/triangles
subjective_question: Are shell edges or typography visibly degraded on the target phone?
pass_rule: Cadence improves without visible loss at normal viewing distance.

hypothesis: One frame authority reduces redundant scheduling and state-phase mismatch.
control: Current R3F bridge plus scheduled fallback rAF
treatment: Cancel fallback when R3F assumes Lenis; derive all state from one sampled progress
locked_variables: device, trace, quality tier
objective_measures: callback count; frame intervals; progress/pose continuity
subjective_question: Does any beat lag or jump relative to scroll?
pass_rule: No continuity regression and no extra rAF callback after ownership transfer.

hypothesis: Hybrid active/demand rendering reduces idle work without a resume hitch.
treatment: demand while stable; continuous only during scroll/theme/pose activity
locked_variables: device, DPR, MSAA, scene, input trace
objective_measures: idle frame count/power proxy; resume first-frame time; warm cadence
subjective_question: Does the first resumed frame pop or stall?
pass_rule: Idle rendering drops materially; resume stays within one measured refresh interval. RESULT: Demand mode stopped cleanly at idle: idle interval 16.7 ms with zero idle renders. Resume smoothness remains a separate active-scroll question.

hypothesis: Physical 120 Hz behavior differs from headless SwiftShader and must be separately validated.
treatment: Same trace on Samsung S25 or equivalent physical 120 Hz device
locked_variables: revision, viewport CSS size, trace duration
objective_measures: measured refresh interval; p50/p95/p99/max; miss streaks; GL facts
subjective_question: Does motion remain temporally even during explode and jump?
pass_rule: No repeated >2x misses; no pose discontinuities; environment clearly labeled.

hypothesis: Predecoding the next poster removes decode hitches from active scroll.
treatment: Fetch and decode next required image outside active scroll; swap on rAF
locked_variables: same image, cache condition, trace
objective_measures: cold decode ms; long frames; frame intervals around swap
subjective_question: Is the swap visually instantaneous and stable?
pass_rule: No frame miss cluster at the swap and no extra eager bytes before need.

hypothesis: Cold shader/PMREM/upload work currently leaks past ready.
treatment: Prewarm hero/explode/jump materials and report ready after first useful compiled frame
locked_variables: device, revision, cache condition
objective_measures: request-to-ready; first useful frame; first-scroll hitch; programs/textures counts
subjective_question: Does first interaction match later interactions?
pass_rule: First trace has no unique compile/upload hitch over warm baseline. RESULT: compileAsync readiness did not prevent the first visible canvas reveal from taking about 6.85 s, and the stall repeated after resize. Ready must include a presented visible-frame gate.

hypothesis: LoAF attribution plus rAF intervals identifies root causes better than FPS alone.
treatment: Add LoAF/longtask attribution and phase marks
locked_variables: trace, device, revision
objective_measures: blockingDuration; script/style/layout attribution; rAF intervals
subjective_question: N/A
pass_rule: Every >50 ms event has attribution or explicit unsupported status. RESULT: The combined report and Chromium trace separated negligible probe CPU cost from software-GPU raster/presentation stalls and recorded environment/concurrency caveats. RESULT: Qualification: the trace excludes large measured probe CPU and reports compositor DroppedFrame 318, but no >50 ms timeline X event identified the GPU wait. Root-cause attribution remains unresolved. RESULT: A controlled 120 ms rAF busy loop produced a LoAF entry, proving the observer works in this Chromium build. Empty application LoAF entries therefore do not mean the API is unsupported, but they still do not identify the visible software-raster or presentation wait.

hypothesis: KTX2 helps only if texture decode/VRAM is material in the GLB.
treatment: KTX2 version if texture audit justifies it
locked_variables: geometry, material appearance, device
objective_measures: bytes; transcode ms; ready ms; textures/VRAM proxy; warm cadence
subjective_question: Are compression artifacts visible on shells or normals?
pass_rule: Lower transfer/VRAM with no worse cold ready and acceptable visual quality. RESULT: Precondition absent: GLB has 38 meshes, 38 primitives, 107684 triangles, and no embedded materials, images, or extensions. KTX2 does not apply unless baked textures are added later.

hypothesis: An extra scroll-to-rAF boundary may add phase latency without reducing event frequency.
control: Passive scroll updates sampled directly by the existing frame authority
treatment: Insert a separate rAF gate before demand invalidation
locked_variables: device, refresh rate, input trace, DPR, scene
objective_measures: target-progress minus rendered-progress; frame intervals; invalidate-to-render delay
subjective_question: Does the rig lag the finger or camera during direction changes?
pass_rule: Do not promote the extra gate unless ordering improves and phase error does not increase.

hypothesis: The multi-second reveal stall is dominated by SwiftShader software raster rather than application CPU work.
treatment: Same build and trace on hardware-accelerated Chrome
locked_variables: viewport, DPR 1.5, revision, cache, input trace
objective_measures: first reveal; reverse p95; qprobe CPU; renderer calls/triangles; GPU identity
subjective_question: Does the visible robot appear promptly and remain coupled to scroll?
pass_rule: If hardware removes the stall while app CPU remains similar, classify the baseline as environment-bound; otherwise continue app diagnosis. RESULT: A post-crash hardware run verified NVIDIA RTX3080Ti WebGL and five visible six-second traces at p95 16.7-16.8ms, worst16.8ms, zero missed intervals and zero long tasks. This removes the earlier multi-second stalls in this environment but host load/restart and prior revisions prevent a strict single-variable causal conclusion. Headless scheduling is60Hz; no S25/120Hz validation.

hypothesis: compileAsync readiness is insufficient because full-size presentation/compositing remains cold.
treatment: Ready only after a representative full-size frame has rendered and presented; repeat after resize
locked_variables: GPU mode, viewport, DPR, scene, revision
objective_measures: compile end; first submitted frame; first presented frame; reveal delay; post-resize reveal
subjective_question: Is the first visible frame immediate, complete, and artifact-free?
pass_rule: Reveal and post-resize presentation complete within one measured refresh interval after ready.

hypothesis: The reveal bottleneck scales with scene raster/draw complexity rather than scroll/state CPU work.
control: Full robot: 70 draw calls, 198412 triangles at DPR 1.5
treatment: Diagnostic render with robot hidden or a trivial proxy while preserving scroll/state scheduling
locked_variables: GPU mode, viewport, DPR, trace, app revision
objective_measures: first reveal; reverse p95; qprobe CPU; render counter
subjective_question: Does removing scene complexity remove the stall without changing state timing?
pass_rule: A large reduction isolates raster/draw cost; no reduction points to compositor/presentation or scheduling. RESULT: Same-build CSS-hidden diagnostic held all five passes at p95 16.7-16.8 ms with zero long tasks and one missed 60 Hz interval total, while visible candidate stayed p95 217-400 ms. This isolates the current software-raster/presentation dependency; hidden output is not a usable smoothness result.

hypothesis: Keeping the full-size canvas at epsilon opacity warms presentation enough to remove the first reveal spike.
treatment: Full-size canvas rendered at opacity 0.001 before reveal
locked_variables: GPU mode, viewport, DPR, scene, revision
objective_measures: first reveal; cold settle; max cold rAF; max long task; reverse p95
subjective_question: Is reveal immediate without a cold-load or steady-scroll regression?
pass_rule: Candidate must remove reveal spike without worsening cold settle or warm cadence. RESULT: Epsilon opacity removed the 6.85 s first-reveal spike, but cold settle worsened from 2.46 s to 4.78 s, max cold rAF reached 1.83 s, max long task 1.70 s, and a pose fix co-landed. No single-factor causal claim.

hypothesis: Batching repeated rigid parts can reduce visible draw submission cost while preserving exact mesh geometry and articulation.
treatment: Instance only repeated geometry+material groups; update per-part matrices from the same rig state
locked_variables: GPU mode, DPR, MSAA, geometry, materials, pose trace
objective_measures: calls; triangles; CPU update; visible frame intervals; continuity
subjective_question: Is the robot pixel-identical at story beats and motion-identical through explode/jump?
pass_rule: Draw calls fall materially, geometry/pose checks pass, and visible cadence improves without cold regression. RESULT: Candidate reduced renderer calls from 70 to 35 while keeping 198412 submitted triangles, but batching and standard-material changes co-landed and the SwiftShader/concurrent-load environment changed. Warm visible p95 generally fell yet remained 200-316.7 ms; no causal cadence pass or independent max-deviation image-parity audit.

hypothesis: A single mesh-UV baked head-shell base-color tile can close the most visible hero-to-live pigment gap without changing geometry or regressing the cold path.
treatment: Bake only material color for the head shell to one 512-square sRGB texture on mesh-space UVs; retain current geometry, MR scalars, camera and lights
locked_variables: exact source mesh/hash, calibrated camera, pose samples, lights, exposure, DPR 1.5, draw batching
objective_measures: encoded bytes; decoded dimensions; texture count; calls/triangles; cold ready; first visible frame; UV seam pixels; registration at rest and head yaw/pitch
subjective_question: Does the printed head artwork stay attached and materially reduce the handoff quality drop at normal phone size?
pass_rule: Pass only if registration holds through motion, calibrated A/B is preferred, draw calls do not rise, decoded cost stays at or below 1 MiB for the proof tile, and cold/first-visible timing has no material regression.

hypothesis: True-metal hardware plus controlled roughness separates mechanism materials.
treatment: Metallic 1 hardware with micro/macro roughness
locked_variables: mesh hash, camera, pose, lights, view transform
objective_measures: preview render time; crop values
subjective_question: Do hardware edges form coherent metallic highlights distinct from paint?
pass_rule: Independent review found improved joint edge readability and material separation.

hypothesis: Sparse multiscale cavities and restrained relief make stone physical without covering labels.
treatment: Three-scale pores plus 5x-reduced quarry relief and label clearance
locked_variables: camera, light, view transform, typography
objective_measures: crop histogram; displacement settings
subjective_question: Does stone read as limestone rather than printed dots or brushed plaster?
pass_rule: Independent review accepted refined preview and clear labels.

hypothesis: Lens-only light linking removes face spill while retaining a readable blue optical cue.
treatment: Link eye lamp only to lens
locked_variables: mesh, camera, all other lights/materials
objective_measures: render time; lens/face crop values; noise
subjective_question: Does the eye read as reflective glass rather than a blue emitter?
pass_rule: No blue face spill; lens remains readable; no material noise regression. RESULT: The 1536x2304 white render retained a readable blue dielectric lens highlight while removing the blue spill previously visible on the ivory face; independent visual review found no new noise regression.

hypothesis: Auxiliary-pass denoising preserves pigment and pores better than automatic denoise alone.
treatment: Noisy image plus albedo/normal Denoise node
locked_variables: seed, samples, camera, materials, lights
objective_measures: 1:1 edge contrast; pore count; render/denoise time
subjective_question: Which output better preserves lettering and fine wear without noise?
pass_rule: Paired review prefers treatment with no unacceptable noise.

hypothesis: An explicit noise threshold spends samples on dark mechanisms and glossy lens more efficiently.
treatment: High max samples with noise threshold 0.01 and controlled min samples
locked_variables: seed, resolution, denoiser, scene
objective_measures: render time pass; sample-count pass; crop noise
subjective_question: Are dark mechanisms and lens cleaner at equal or lower time?
pass_rule: Equal/better crop quality within current render-time budget.

hypothesis: Light-group tuning can increase form without material confounds.
treatment: A/B key/fill/rim group weights in compositor
locked_variables: materials, geometry, sampling, exposure, AgX
objective_measures: patch luminance; clipping; render reuse
subjective_question: Does mechanism depth improve while labels and ivory retain detail?
pass_rule: Review prefers treatment and no patch clipping.

hypothesis: A persistent real set and shared camera/robot progress make angle change, jump, landing-triggered explode, and set departure read as one spatial sequence.
control: Rejected whole-scene opacity fade and flat hero handoff; retain its captures as diagnostic history only.
treatment: Real Blender set meshes, one traveling camera, continuous robot rig, touchdown-owned explode onset, and geometric set exit.
locked_variables: robot source geometry; theme at each comparison; viewport 360/430; DPR; light/exposure per theme; source revision; deterministic progress trace
objective_measures: eight checkpoint images; every-frame canvas/set opacity; set world matrices; projected anchors and bounds; foot-to-support separation; explode onset; forward/reverse identity; texture and draw budgets; cold/warm timing
subjective_question: Does the duck visibly land and cause the explode while the same real set moves out of view with depth?
pass_rule: All spatial-frontier.md M16 assertions must pass at both widths; no scene fade; explode=0 before touchdown; immediate post-contact onset; continuous paths; same geometry and reverse identity. A headless run cannot prove physical 120 Hz. RESULT: User rejected the whole-scene fade and selected camera angle change, duck jump, touchdown-triggered explode and geometric set exit. Real set export and browser implementation are in progress; checkpoint and performance results are not yet available. RESULT: Three bounded actual-set prototypes now preserve set object identity, matrices and opacity; corrected .56 impact onset and reverse/static reduced-motion states pass. Earlier jump/head/spec collisions were corrected. Final scenic props still remain behind specs in prototype3, so camera departure and actual baked robot materials remain under refinement before dense frames/timings.

hypothesis: One shared 1024-square PBR atlas can preserve set pigment and material cues with lower material/binding cost than per-object maps.
control: Same exported real set with per-object textures, identical visible texel target and channel set.
treatment: One shared 1024-square base-color atlas with matching packed MR and only justified normal data; UV margins retained.
locked_variables: set and robot geometry; camera eight checkpoints; light rig; exposure; theme; texture filtering; DPR; hardware renderer; image comparison regions
objective_measures: encoded bytes; decoded texel bytes plus mip chain; channels/textures/materials; renderer calls/triangles; cold decode/upload; first visible frame; seams and print legibility at phone size
subjective_question: Do podium pores, printed banner and maker text stay attached and readable at oblique camera angles without appearing as flat cards?
pass_rule: Use identical channel sets for budget comparison. Reject a texture at 1024 if labels or seams fail phone-size review; document per-object fallback and measured cost. No geometry replacement, no baked moving contact shadow, and no performance promotion without cold/warm evidence.

hypothesis: Lossless attribute/index coding reduces transfer while preserving the official source geometry byte-for-byte.
control: Original robot surface GLB with deterministic gzip.
treatment: EXT_meshopt_compression v0 with NONE filters, no quantization or reorder, then deterministic gzip.
locked_variables: Identical 75 original buffer views, indices, textures, JSON semantics, gzip level and geometry identity.
objective_measures: Encoded bytes; exact decoded bytes for every view; decoder requirement.
subjective_question: No visual change is permitted.
pass_rule: Every decoded geometry byte equals the control and final transported size improves. RESULT: Identity passed on 9209280 bytes. Payload failed: 7991460 versus 7492826 bytes, a 498634-byte regression before decoder cost. Rejected; retain ordinary gzip.
